scenes.title: Cash-and-Carry vs Reverse Cash-and-Carry
scenes.concept: Detail two-sided arbitrage strategies when market forward price departs from theoretical parity.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Cash-and-Carry: If market forward is overpriced, borrow, buy spot, and sell forward
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Reverse Cash-and-Carry: If forward is underpriced, short spot, lend cash, and buy forward
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Arbitrage forces market prices to converge instantly to theoretical parity
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Forward Price with Known Cash Income
scenes.concept: Formulate F_0 = (S_0 - I) * e^(rT) showing how interim cash flows reduce forward carry cost.

scenes.title: Forward Price with Continuous Dividend Yield
scenes.concept: Compare no-dividend assets with continuous yield assets: F_0 = S_0 * e^((r - q)*T).

beatOutlines.textOutline: Continuous dividend yield q offsets financing cost r directly in exponent
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Net cost of carry equals (r - q)
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When dividend yield exceeds interest rate (q > r), forward trades below spot

scenes.concept: Execute strict 8-step summary sequence covering all chapter principles with dedicated Rule 8 focus.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Executive overview of all eight forward pricing principles

beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rules 3 & 4: Forward formula F_0 = S_0 * e^(rT) and two-sided cash-and-carry bounds
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rules 5 & 6: Known cash income adjustment and continuous dividend yield pricing

beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Final 2-column whole-chapter reference matrix
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: 1. Asset Classification: Investment assets allow two-way arbitrage; consumption assets only define upper bounds.
2. Short Selling Rules: Short sellers must remit all dividends to lenders and provide collateral margin.
3. Spot-Forward Parity: F_0 = S_0 * e^(rT) represents the cost of financing spot storage until maturity.
4. Cash-and-Carry Bounds: Divergence from parity triggers instant riskless borrowing and spot replication.
5. Known Cash Income: Interim cash payments reduce forward prices: F_0 = (S_0 - I) * e^(rT).
6. Continuous Dividend Yield: Continuous dividends offset financing costs: F_0 = S_0 * e^((r - q)*T).
7. Kidder Peabody Disaster: Software failure to discount forward STRIPs created $350M in phantom profits.
8. Repo Special Squeezes: High short interest drives repo rates negative and triggers violent forced buy-ins.
bottomTakeaway: Forward prices represent the no-arbitrage cost of carry, not market forecasts; dividend income reduces carry costs, and proper discounting is vital.
